ideas: Which family member and the traits you share
A moment when the similarity was obvious
Whether you're happy to be like them

phrases.meaning: look or behave like an older relative

phrases.phrase: a chip off the old block

model: The person in my family who I'm most similar to is definitely my dad. Everyone says I take after him, and my aunt always jokes that I'm a chip off the old block. He's an engineer who works for a construction company in Hanoi, and he's the kind of man who plans everything, and in that way we have a lot in common. For example, before any trip, he makes a spreadsheet that lists every hotel, bus and restaurant, and I'm doing the same thing right now for my holiday next month. Being organised seems to run in the family. We're also both quite stubborn, which means we don't always see eye to eye. When we argue about politics or money at dinner, it can get pretty loud, and my mum says we get on each other's nerves because we're too alike rather than too different. I remember one moment last Tet, when we were both trying to fix the same broken light in the kitchen, each insisting on our own method, and my mum just burst out laughing. My dad's getting a bit set in his ways now that he's older, and I'm a little worried I'll end up the same. But generally I'm quite happy to be like him. He's honest, hard-working and reliable, and deep down he has a soft spot for everyone in the family. If I become half the person he is, I'll be satisfied.
